This happened on a Tuesday night, and I still can't believe how dumb it was.
I was getting ready for bed, already in my pajamas, when I remembered I hadn't taken the trash out.
It was already pretty late, almost eleven, but the trash truck comes early on Wednesdays, so I figured I'd just run it out real quick before I forgot completely.
I didn't bother putting on shoes or grabbing my keys.
I mean, it's just the driveway, right?
How long could it take, ten seconds, maybe fifteen?
I picked up the bag, walked outside in my socks, and dropped it in the bin by the curb.
Easy.
Except when I turned around to go back inside, the door had already shut behind me.
And it was locked.
Not just closed, actually locked, the kind that doesn't budge no matter how many times you try the handle.
I stood there for a second, just staring at the door like it was going to magically open if I looked at it long enough.
It didn't.
I checked my pockets, but of course, no phone, no keys, nothing.
Just me, my pajamas, and an empty trash bin sitting on the curb like it was mocking me.
I started walking around the house, checking every window, every door, hoping something, anything, was unlocked.
Nothing was.
Not even the little side window I usually forget to lock.
My neighbor's porch light was on, so I figured I'd ask to use their phone.
But then I looked down at what I was wearing, and honestly, I almost turned back around and just sat on my own porch until morning.
I mean, my pajamas had little cartoon ducks all over them, the kind my sister bought me as a joke last Christmas.
Not exactly what you want to be wearing when you knock on a stranger's door at eleven at night.
But I didn't really have another option, so I took a deep breath and walked over and knocked.
The guy who opened the door just looked at me for a second, then looked down at the ducks, and then back up at me, clearly trying to decide if I was someone he should be worried about.
He didn't say anything about it, which honestly, I really appreciated.
He just let me use his phone, and I called my roommate, who was thankfully still awake and only mildly confused by the whole thing.
It took her about fifteen minutes to get home and let me in.
Fifteen minutes standing on a stranger's porch in duck pajamas, waving awkwardly every time a car drove by, wondering how many neighbors were watching from their windows.
The next morning, I told my roommate we needed a spare key hidden somewhere outside, immediately, no more excuses.
She just laughed and said, "Or you could just wear pants next time." Fair point.
Now I keep a key under a fake rock by the porch, and I never, ever take the trash out without my phone again.
